cases.scope: Export-license condition applies to individuals whose most recent country of citizenship or permanent residence is Cuba, Iran, North Korea, Syria, or the named Ukrainian territories. It is not a general sponsorship refusal or a citizenship-only rule.
cases.timing: For affected applicants, the posting says processing times are extended and/or licenses are routinely denied, so the required license will not be granted by the summer internship start date. No separate current-versus-future sponsorship policy is stated.

evidence.locator: public question description: Would you require an export license under the circumstances described below?
evidence.text: Internships at Waymo, including those outside the US, involve access to information regulated by US export control laws. These laws require that export controlled information cannot be shared without an export license to individuals whose most recent country of citizenship or permanent residence is Cuba, Iran, North Korea, Syria or Ukrainian territories: Crimea, the so-called Donetsk People's Republic ("DNR"), and the so-called Luhansk People's Republic ("LNR"). Please understand that applications for these licenses have extended processing times and/or are routinely denied by the U.S. government such that the required license will not be granted by the summer internship start date.

cases.title: Software Engineering Internship (Summer 2027)
cases.scope: The internship requires access to ITAR-regulated information and expressly requires all applicants to be U.S. persons. This is an eligibility restriction, not a stated sponsorship policy.
cases.exceptions: The posting defines U.S. person to include U.S. citizens, U.S. permanent residents (green-card holders), and protected persons under 8 U.S.C. 1324b(a)(3). The same rule appears in the application question description.

completeness.note: Official job description and public application question descriptions retrieved; no application responses or personal data retrieved.

evidence.text: This position requires use of information which is subject to the International Traffic in Arms Regulations (ITAR). All applicants must be U.S. persons within the meaning of ITAR. ITAR defines a US person as: any individual who is granted U.S. citizenship; or. any individual who is granted U.S. permanent residence ("Green Card" holder); or. any individual who is granted status as a "protected person" under 8 U.S.C 1324b(a)(3).
